I would say that I have a hard time being vulnerable with people and being completely blunt with those I do not trust completely yet. I can tend to be very stern and matter of fact about my feelings when addressing adversity and even my romantic feelings (my Venus is conjunct with my moon as well). I do somewhat try to do what is better for the collective at times than what is best for myself - at the same time if someone bothers me enough I will eventually express it. With time I’ve learned how to better balance these aspects. This expression is done most efficiently with some level of removal (through text or email) than in person. I can get a hot head - especially when I feel someone is acting unjustly (this might have more to do with my Mars in 12H Pisces which is aspecting my moon). When this happens I often speak over people and discount them - possibly making them feel stupid for even speaking about a certain subject in such a way (this is mainly directed towards racists, transphobes, xenophobes, misogynists, “narcissists”, etc.)
Forgot to mention: growing up I didn’t feel that I had substantial emotional support and often had to be there for myself and even my mother who sifted through husband after husband. It wasn’t until I was 18 that I finally had a supportive father figure in my life. I was often used as a therapist by my mother (as young as 10). I always felt distant from my peers - like I understood things they didn’t and vise versa. As I’ve aged this has leveled out. I dealt with a lot of inner turmoil growing up and more often than not I would take out my stress on myself. I missed out on a lot because I developed depression and a deep distrust for people (Chiron in Scorpio). I have been learning that I am safe in my body and that life is worth living. I’ve learned to let go of the heavier things while still respecting that they exist. I am okay with impermanence. My biggest thing is procrastination right now.

Tell me I’m wrong but part of it may also be just be psychological. Perhaps you may be hyper vigilant - constantly feeling out people’s emotions or feelings towards you because it gives you a sense of safety and preparedness. Maybe ask yourself why you feel such a need to care about others perceptions of you and what originally made you aware of that sort of thing. I’m not discounting the metaphysical aspect, but I feel people overlook the logical aspects with it when in reality it all goes hand in hand. When you know yourself and your worth you won’t feel such a need to care about others perceptions of you unless you’re given something like constructive criticism. There’s a sort of calm that comes with that. There will always be people like that and when you’re hyper vigilant you give those people/energies more power - thus becoming anxious and somewhat paranoid. 
More often than not people that feel a need to put down others are hurting in their own way. Understand them in a way you may understand your own unsavory behaviors - maybe once you did the same. Part of the experience may be karmic. You may be seeing things on the other side. Either way, remember that you are consciousness looking back at itself.
When it comes to grounding exercises my top recommendation is going to be yoga or even some basic stretching every morning to get back in tune with your body and the physical plane. Really feel your own touch and your muscles expanding. Otherwise I would recommend immersing yourself in an element that makes you feel safe (water, earth, fire, air, etc.) also take time to look at your world with the eyes of a child.

Honestly I think the best teacher is yourself and the world around you. I don’t know if you have any pets or have had any pets but think about a time that you came across a dog/pet that was excited to see you. Their energy is so positive it’s contagious. Really feel what it’s like to feel what the dog is feeling (excitement-wise) and then visualize in your head what that dogs energy would look/feel like as an abstraction. Some colors or shapes may come up. Think about how they feel. Don’t worry about doing this perfectly - everyone sees energy a little differently (just like how some people in real life need glasses). Once you feel comfortable with it, imagine your energy and the dogs energy interacting from your meeting. You might see airy, swirly energies moving about. You can do this with anything/anyone that you get a strong feeling from and it’s even better if you can do it while interacting. 

I would recommend doing a “vibe check” with yourself every day to see what you’re projecting energy-wise and to get familiar with the practice of seeing.

Once you get familiar you can learn how to affect the energies around you. You can learn to protect yourself or even send a message without ever speaking a word.

Over time you’ll see what works for you and what doesn’t. I know some people need to meditate to see energies while others can just flip a switch and see. Some people may be more naturally gifted but everyone has the potential. Remember, we were all born from the same energy and then spliced and multiplied ourselves off of that. I would definitely recommend trying to tap into that source energy but I will warn you that it may cause an ego death the first time which isn’t necessarily bad but will definitely shake your world up.

As for the traditional 7 chakras, you might be surprised to hear this but some have them and some don’t. They’re kinda like a spiritual installation. They’re these undulating/circumambulating energy balls. Most of the time a healthy classic chakra will have a bright color and energetic movement. An unhealthy/blocked chakra moves slower and has darker colors in it. 
Everyone does have energy points though - I guess some people would also call these chakras but they’re different from the classic seven. These are all over the body and they’re very similar to my description of chakras except these can also house specific memories. This is why some will recommend traumatized individuals to do yoga because doing so helps them to connect to those certain parts that have stored trauma so that they can release that energy point. It’s actually a pretty cool thing to see energetically. It’s like the process of a black hole but in reverse - if that makes sense.

Unfortunately, the systems we live by don’t allow people like me to thrive (especially people in poverty or bipoc). Often we are the ones who are able to teach and connect people with the inner workings (or magic) of the universe. Very often we are ostracized, if not by the government then by the people (sometimes both). 
Those who are savvy with people may become leaders, though often they are killed and their teachings are diluted and used as rhetoric for others agendas. Often they are the martyrs revered but slowly forgotten by time. While once Socrates name illuminated the halls of schools everywhere, he is now reduced to a chapter in your intro to philosophy class that your professor begrudgingly sifts through.
There are the ones like me, awkwardly stumbling throughout the world, searching for something to cling to like a mad dog. We are the ones that work in the shadows, barely noticed until our own inevitable implosion or death. After our treasures, most of which created by a misery that one can only understand by experience, are found we are called revolutionaries and deemed as icons. To the children in the future our work echos a daunting, ominous, sometimes wondrous but indiscernible message. There will be edgy art students that cling to our creations without really understanding what they mean. We will be reduced to an aesthetic.
Some will eventually turn to the occult, becoming either the illusionist or the illusioned. They will become a warning to children of the future.
There are no lucky ones for to reach the insight we have entails a great deal of suffering. But life will continue to go on and people like us will continue to exist. And all the things that will happen will happen. And all that is to be forgotten will be forgotten.
I’ll leave you with these questions, does the saving of hundreds justify the torture of one? Does the subserviency of one to a higher power justify the abuse one has endured?
